Two years ago, when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports immediately brought good news: the built-in SSD was not soldered onto the logic board. This allowed users to upgrade the storage capacity themselves, and we demonstrated how to do it at the time.

However, the newly released M6 and M5 Pro versions of the Mac mini appear to have the storage chips soldered onto the logic board once again.

The return to a soldered design for the storage chips in the new Mac mini is a major step backwards

The team at Expand Mac mini revealed in a blog post that the NAND chips on the new machine have been soldered onto the logic board, a situation similar to the M1 and M2 versions of the Mac mini, meaning the SSD module cannot be removed.

Expand Mac mini has been selling storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro versions of the Mac mini. However, they stated that the chances of support for the "M6 and M5 Pro appear to be rather slim at the moment."

With no slots there is nothing to replace, and the room left for us is also very limited. Back in August this year we mentioned that we would expand the range of support after testing the actual machines. These are the test results, but not what we had hoped for. We will continue to look for feasible solutions, but the chances of support for the M6 and M5 Pro appear to be rather slim. If there are any changes, we will notify everyone here at the first opportunity.

For comparison, the 1TB SSD expansion module launched by Expand Mac mini for the M4 Mac mini is priced at US$300. Apple charges US$500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module is priced at US$420, while Apple's similar upgrade costs US$1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guide still shows that the SSD is designed to be removable. However, no teardown reports have been seen so far to confirm this.

Although it cannot replace an internal storage upgrade, Satechi has launched a cleverly designed accessory with a built-in SSD enclosure and additional ports, suitable for the M6 Mac mini.
